# Anonymous Submissions store no person and no time, and are unlinkable at rest, not against a restore

**Threat model.** The Lead, Organization admins, and anyone using the product (UI, API, exports) must never be able to link a member to their Submission, and neither can an operator reading stored data, dumps, or R2 backups. We do **not** claim to defend against an operator who restores the Durable Object to a past moment (point-in-time recovery replays every write, including the one transaction that writes a Participation record and its Submission), reads Cloudflare's internal edge logs, or changes the code to start logging. Against that we use controls instead: only named people can trigger a restore, the privacy page states the 30-day restore window, and code changes on the submission path need review. The answer page's "Your name is never stored with your answers" is true of everything stored.

**Design.**
- Everything lives in the Organization's Durable Object. There is no per-Round object. The first Answer writes the Participation record and a Submission holding that one Answer in **one transaction**, which is how a double submission is rejected (a unique Participation record per Round and Person).
- An anonymous Submission stores only its Round, its Answers, and an Edit key hash. It stores **no person, no Invitation, and no time at all**, not even the day SPEC allows. A Participation record stores Round, Person, and the fact of answering, also with no time.
- Submission and Answer tables are `WITHOUT ROWID` with random 128-bit keys. Reads aggregate or sort by the random key. Dumps and backups are written in key order.
- **The anonymous Submission table has no person column, ever.** Attributed Submissions get their own table, so no bug can put a name on an anonymous answer.
- The Invitation token travels in the **URL fragment**, so the answer page GET (and every link scanner) never sends it. The page POSTs it to a **separate Submission Worker** with logs, traces, tail, Logpush, and Analytics Engine writes all off. That Worker logs error codes only. Tokens are stored only as hashes.
- The **browser generates the Edit key** and sends only its SHA-256 hash with the first Answer. Later Answers and changes carry only the Edit key. **No request may carry both an Invitation token and an Edit key**, and the server rejects one that does.

## Considered Options

- **Submissions in a separate Durable Object.** Rejected: without one transaction, a crash either loses the Answer or allows a second Submission, and the timing gap still exists.
- **Shuffled batch writes.** Rejected: buffered Answers are lost if the object is evicted, and it defends only against the restore threat we don't claim to cover.
- **A nullable person column shared with attributed mode.** Rejected: a single bug would put names on anonymous answers.

## Consequences

Response and answer counts come from Participation records. Answer latency is measured only in tests on a preview stage. Deleting a Person deletes their Participation records, and their anonymous Submissions survive. A member who loses the Edit key cannot change their answers, and that is accepted.
# A one-tap rating link only preselects; the answer is saved when the member confirms it

SPEC §5.1 said each rating link in an email "records the answer". Email security scanners (Microsoft Defender runs headless Chrome) fetch every link, so recording on GET would count scanners as voters. Some scanners can also produce trusted events, so saving on any interaction would still be unsafe. A rating link (`/a#t=<token>&v=<1–5>`) therefore opens the answer page with that value preselected and writes nothing. The answer is saved only when the member taps "Save and continue", which sits directly under the anonymity statement, or changes the value. A member who taps in the email and leaves without touching the page loses that answer. We accept that loss as the price of never counting a scanner.

## Consequences

- The token exchange that loads the page has no side effects, so R1 has no open tracking at all.
- The anonymity statement is always read before the first Answer is stored.
- One-tap needs a rating Question first in the Pulse. Otherwise the email offers only "Open check-in".
# Workspace layout and toolchain: pnpm, TypeScript 7, oxc tools, and Alchemy v2's Effect runtime kept inside the adapters

> Partly superseded by ADR 0011 (the app entry uses Foldkit, not React and Base UI), ADR 0012 (`packages/cloudflare` depends on `packages/emails`), and ADR 0013 (domain folder layout). The rest stands.

**Workspace.** pnpm workspaces with a `catalog:` of exact pins, on Node 24 LTS (`.node-version`). Pinned at: `effect` and all `@effect/*` 4.1.2, `alchemy` and `@alchemy.run/*` 2.0.0-beta.85, `typescript` 7.0.2, and exact `oxlint`, `oxlint-tsgolint`, and `oxfmt` versions. The Effect and Alchemy pins move only together, in a PR of their own, because both are marked unstable or beta.

**Packages.**

| Package | Holds | May depend on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/domain` | Schemas and services by concept (`people/`, `pulses/`, `rounds/`, `answering/`, `results/`, `actions/`, `privacy/`), schedule and Result calculations | `effect` only |
| `packages/api` | The HttpApi declaration shared by server and client | `domain` |
| `packages/cloudflare` | Adapters (Organization DO, D1, Queue consumer, `EmailSender`, alarm scheduler) and the two Worker entries: the main Worker and the Submission Worker | `domain`, `api`, Alchemy runtime |
| `apps/web` | One Vite 8 project with two entries: the app (React, TanStack Router, Base UI) and the answer page (no React, no HttpApi client: plain `fetch` plus shared Schemas) | `api`, `domain` (Schemas) |
| `packages/emails` | Email templates | `domain` |
| `infra` | The Alchemy stack and stages (`pr-<n>`, `staging`, `production`) | everything |

**Cloudflare runtime.** Workers, the Durable Object, the Queue consumer, and Cron are defined with Alchemy v2's Effect runtime, but only in `packages/cloudflare`. If the beta fails us, replacing it with a hand-written bridge of about 100 lines touches only that package.

**Tooling.**
- TypeScript 7.0.2 (the native compiler) with `tsc -b` and project references. Settings: `strict`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`.
- `@effect/tsgo` provides Effect diagnostics.
- oxfmt formats. oxlint lints, with type-aware rules from `oxlint-tsgolint`.
- A local `jsPlugins` package, `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat`, bans `cloudflare:*` and Alchemy imports in `domain` and `api`, and holds the privacy query lint (no `rowid`, no unordered reads of anonymous tables, no joins between anonymous tables and Participation or Invitation).
- The boundary is also enforced by dependencies: `domain` declares only `effect` and uses `types: []`.

**Tests.** Vitest with `@effect/vitest` everywhere:
- domain and API tests in plain Node with in-memory layers and `HttpApiTest`;
- adapter tests through `@alchemy.run/test` `Test.make({ dev: true })` on local workerd;
- smoke tests with `Test.make()` on the PR stage;
- Playwright end-to-end tests on the PR stage.

`vitest-pool-workers` is not used, and there is no hand-edited wrangler config.

**Answer entry (measured in the answer-page prototype, 2026-11-07).** The answer entry is prerendered static HTML with inline CSS and a small plain TypeScript controller, with no React, Preact, or Base UI. Measured with Lighthouse mobile (slow 4G, 4× CPU), the time until the Question text appears was 1.12 s with this approach, 1.35 s with Preact, 1.61 s with React, and 1.90 s with React plus Base UI. The token request starts from an inline script in `<head>`, and Effect Schema (23.5 KB gzip) loads after first paint. Budget: JS ≤ 10 KB gzip on the critical path, CSS ≤ 2 KB inline, HTML ≤ 8 KB, 1 request before first paint and 2 before the Question text. A Lighthouse CI gate checks FCP ≤ 800 ms, LCP ≤ 1.3 s, and TBT ≤ 50 ms.

## Considered Options

- **TypeScript 5.9 or 6.** Rejected: 7.0.2 is npm `latest`, Effect recommends it, and Alchemy is built against it. 6.0 is the end of the JavaScript-based compiler line. Our tools (oxc, Vite/rolldown, Vitest) don't depend on the old compiler API.
- **Biome, or ESLint with Prettier.** Rejected in favour of oxlint and oxfmt. oxlint's `jsPlugins` let the boundary and privacy rules be ordinary lint rules, and `oxlint-tsgolint` gives type-aware rules on TypeScript 7.
- **A hand-written Effect bridge from day one.** Deferred: Alchemy's runtime removes the bridge code. Keeping it in one package makes the switch cheap if we need it.

## Consequences

A spike on a preview stage verifies this before the walking skeleton is built. It checks the Organization DO with `SqliteClient`, transactions, migrations, and an alarm, a Queue consumer with a dead-letter queue, the Submission Worker with every log setting off, the deployed cold start, and `tsc -b` with project references on TypeScript 7.0.2.

# A member's history page reads past answers only from their own browser

The member's private history page lists the Rounds the member took part in, from their Participation records, which the server already holds with a Person and no answers (ADR 0005). Their own past answers come only from their own browser: when the answer page saves a Submission, it also keeps the member's answers in local storage next to the Edit key, for one year, and the member can clear them. For each Round the page shows the member's own answer beside the Team's score, but only once the Result is shared and the aggregate meets the minimum group size.

The server never learns which Submission is the member's. A new device or cleared browser data shows the Rounds without answers, and the page says why.

## Considered options

- **Server-side history encrypted with a key only the member holds:** rejected for Release 2. Key recovery across devices is hard to get right, and any server-side record of a member's answers, encrypted or not, weakens the A1–A10 invariants (ADR 0005) that the privacy suite proves.
- **Only the Team's Results the member took part in, no own answers:** too little to be worth a page.

## Consequences

- Answers stay on one device. The page must state this plainly.
- Comments are kept in the browser as the member typed them, not redacted; they never leave the device.
- Clearing site data or a private window loses the history. Nothing on the server can restore it.

# A test Invitation is its own token kind, and its answers are never saved

A Lead or Organization admin can send themselves a test of a Pulse from the Pulse editor (issue #136). The test is the real Invitation email in the sender's language, with "Test" in the subject, the same one-tap rating links, and the real answer page. The flow runs to the end, including the "Your Lead will see: …" preview and the thank-you screen, but it stores no Submission, no Answer, and no Participation record, so nothing reaches Results, Comment themes, or member history. This amends the ADR 0005 flow for one new token kind. It does not weaken A1–A10.

**Token kind.**
- A test token is derived from `INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY` like an Invitation token, but under its own label: `test-invitation:v1:<pulseId>:<personId>:<testId>`, where `testId` is random per send. A test token can therefore never equal an Invitation token, and the key still never leaves the Worker environment.
- Only the token's hash is stored, in its own D1 table `test_invitation_index` (hash, Organization, Pulse, expiry). It is never written to `invitation_index`, and the Organization has no Invitation row for it. A test token expires 7 days after it is sent.
- The Organization stores only the send in `test_send` (send id, Person, Pulse, token hash, time) for the rate limit and for the Queue consumer to index the token once the email is sent, as it does for Invitations. Rows older than 7 days are deleted.

**Answering with a test token.**
- `/exchange` resolves `invitation_index` first. A miss falls back to `test_invitation_index`, and the Organization builds the context from the Pulse's saved Questions and settings, with `test: true`, no Round, `hasAnswered: false`, and the expiry as close time.
- `/first-answer` with a test token applies every check the real route applies (body-only credentials, A5, Edit key hash format). It then redacts the comment as the real path would, returns `{ saved: true, shownToLead }`, and writes nothing to the Organization. It records the Edit key hash in D1's `test_submission_index` (hash, Organization, Pulse, expiry), never in `submission_index`.
- `/answer` resolves `submission_index` first. A miss falls back to `test_submission_index`, and the answer is redacted and discarded the same way.
- The routes that write Submissions and Participation records (`recordFirstAnswer`, `saveAnswer`) are reachable only through `invitation_index` and `submission_index`, so a test token or a test Edit key cannot write a real answer. The privacy suite proves it.
- The answer page shows "This is a test. Your answers aren't saved." It keeps the test Edit key in memory only and does not keep the answers in the browser, so the member history page (ADR 0017) never shows a test.

**Who and how often.** Whoever may edit the Pulse (the Team's Lead and Organization admins, `team.editPulse`) may send a test, to their own address only. The Organization refuses a sixth send by the same Person within an hour. Non-production stages capture the email in D1, as for every other email.

## Considered options

- **A test Round with real Invitations, deleted afterwards.** Rejected: it would write Participation records and Submissions, and any missed cleanup leaks into Results and response rates.
- **A flag on the Invitation token or on `invitation_index`.** Rejected: one missed check would let a test write a real answer. Separate tables make the real write path unreachable.
- **Opening the answer page with a preview flag and no email.** Rejected: the Lead wants to see exactly what members get, including the email and its one-tap links.

## Consequences

- The Submission Worker reads two more D1 tables, and both hold hashes only, with no Person.
- Test answers are lost by design. The Lead cannot see them, and neither can anyone else.
- `test_send` stores a Person and a time, but nothing about answers.

content.text:
I built "Send me a test" for issue #136 and opened PR #144. It is not merged: CI checks had not finished when I stopped, and I didn't wait on them.

- **ADR 0021:** a test Invitation is its own token kind. Its token is derived under a separate label (`test-invitation:v1:`). Only hashes are stored, in their own D1 tables (`test_invitation_index`, `test_submission_index`). So the code that writes Submissions and Participation records can't be reached with a test token. Test answers are redacted for the "Your Lead will see" preview and then thrown away. A1–A10 are unchanged.
- **What was built:**
  - A "Send me a test" button in the Pulse editor for the Team's Lead and Organization admins. It emails only the person who clicked, in their language.
  - The new endpoint, classified in `PrivacyRegistry.ts`, with a server-side limit of 5 sends per Person per hour (the 6th gets a 429).
  - The email has "Test:" in the subject, a test notice and no delivery-time link.
  - The token exchange returns the Pulse's saved Questions with `test: true`. First-answer and answer return success but never write anything.
  - The answer page shows the test banner and test thank-you text. It keeps no Edit key or answers in the browser, so member history never shows a test.
  - English and German copy.
- **Deviations:**
  - The test email's footer says the sender sent it to themselves, not "you are a member of the team".
  - Expired test rows in D1 are deleted whenever a new test goes out.
  - The 429 error is listed on every Pulse endpoint, not just the new one, because they all share one error type.
- **Reviewer findings:** no blocking or major issues in any slice. I fixed the cleanup of expired test rows. I left as minor:
  - A send result can show briefly on another Pulse if you switch Pulses mid-send.
  - The answer page's test mode has no automated test, because that page has no test harness.
- **Tests:** all pass, including both typechecks, lint, format check, the web build, both locale pages within budget, and the workerd tests `Organization.test.ts`, `SubmissionWorker.test.ts` and `Email.test.ts` run singly.
  - Unit: 934.
  - Privacy: 235, including new cases proving a test token never creates or changes a Submission or Participation.
- **Not done yet:** I have not tried the flow on a deployed stage.

PR https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/pull/144, head 06b7b599, checks and reviews pending. Squash-merge with `gh pr merge 144 --squash --delete-branch` once checks are green.
